name: Abstract algebra: patterns of moves
description: Groups, rings and fields: the rules behind clocks, hatches, tiles and codes, taught at the Kepler outpost.
about:
Abstract algebra realm ("Abstract algebra: patterns of moves"): groups, subgroups, homomorphisms, group actions, rings and fields,
for an adult who has finished Foundations and Linear algebra. Same Kepler outpost, now the Vault Works, where the crew builds dials,
hatches, floors and vault doors. In every one only the pattern of moves matters. Mira is still the mentor. The concept plan is
docs/plans/ABSTRACT-PLAN.md.

chapters.name: Clock arithmetic and groups
chapters.blurb: Adding and multiplying on a clock, operation tables, identities, inverses and the rules that make a group.

sector.name: Lock Workshop
sector.purpose: build locks whose dials always come back round

chapters.name: Order and cycles
chapters.blurb: How many steps an element takes to come home, cyclic groups and their generators.

sector.name: Beacon Tower
sector.purpose: time every beacon to repeat on a fixed beat

chapters.name: Permutations and symmetry
chapters.blurb: Rearrangements, cycles, even and odd moves, and the symmetries of a regular polygon.

sector.name: Hatch Hall
sector.purpose: turn and flip every hatch without losing track

chapters.name: Subgroups and cosets
chapters.blurb: Groups inside groups, the cosets that tile a group, and Lagrange's theorem.

sector.name: Sorting Depot
sector.purpose: split every stock of parts into equal, matching batches

chapters.name: Maps between groups
chapters.blurb: Homomorphisms, kernels and images, isomorphisms, products and quotient groups.

sector.name: Relay Exchange
sector.purpose: pass patterns between systems without breaking them

chapters.name: Groups in action
chapters.blurb: Orbits and stabilisers, conjugacy classes, Burnside's counting and abelian groups.

sector.name: Tile Studio
sector.purpose: count every truly different design for the dome floors

chapters.name: Rings and fields
chapters.blurb: Two operations at once: rings, fields, polynomials, ideals and finite fields.

sector.name: Cipher Vault
sector.purpose: build a number system we can always divide in

copy.homeTitle:
Every lock has a pattern.
Learn the rules behind it.
copy.firstVisit: Welcome to the Vault Works. Every dial, hatch and floor tile here follows a few simple rules, and once you know them you can predict any combination of moves. We start with a dial that counts round like a clock.
copy.allDone: Every lock, hatch and vault here now runs on rules you can prove. Number theory opens next in the Signal Office, where these clocks become codes.
copy.chaptersNote: Seven chapters. Learn every concept in a chapter to unlock a landmark for the outpost. Practice missions are optional.

skills.title: The skill tree
skills.text: Follow the prerequisite branches from clock sums to fields. Each mission you finish opens the ideas that are built on it.

visual.title: The concept bench
visual.text: Pick any mission, change its numbers and predict the answer before you check it. Nothing here affects your progress, and it all works offline.

help.title: Look for the pattern of moves, not the parts.
help.intro: Abstract algebra starts where Linear algebra ends: with a set of things, one or two ways to combine them, and a few simple rules. It teaches how to spot the same pattern in clocks, hatches, tiles and codes, and why one pattern can be a copy of another. Every new word and symbol is explained before you are asked to use it, with a worked example first.
help.answers: Answers are numbers: a remainder from 0 to n − 1, a size, a count, an order, or a sign typed as 1 or -1. A permutation is never typed; you are asked where one symbol goes. A yes or no is typed as 1 or 0.
